title: Frozen Coffee Drink with Whipped Cream

content.title: About
content.content: The frozen coffee drink with whipped cream is a refreshing dessert beverage made from cold espresso, milk, sugar, and a generous swirl of whipped cream. It is served as a thick, icy slush, often in a tall glass with a straw.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first frozen coffee drinks appeared in the United States in the early 1990s as a twist on traditional ice cream.
Whipped cream adds not only flavor but also the characteristic “fluffy” texture.
Variations may include flavorings such as vanilla, caramel, mint, or chocolate.
The drink is frequently topped with sprinkles, chocolate shavings, or caramel drizzle.
Although most popular in summer, many cafés serve it year‑round.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: Whipped cream provides calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee is rich in B2 and B3 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: The combination of sweetness and caffeine can lift mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake may cause anxiety, insomnia, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugar increases calories and may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Whipped cream contains lactose, which can cause discomfort for intolerant individuals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to the cream.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen coffee drink with whipped cream immediately after preparation to preserve its creamy texture. Feel free to add sprinkles, syrups, or fruit toppings to suit your taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. For best quality, consume within 1–2 weeks; longer storage may cause ice crystal formation.
